{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2020}} {{Infobox military unit | unit_name = Twelfth United States Army Group | image = 12th Army Group.svg | image_size = 150px | caption = Shoulder sleeve insignia | dates = 1944–45 | country = {{flagicon|USA}} [[United States]] | branch = {{army|United States}} | type = [[Army group]] | role = Army Group [[Headquarters#Military|Headquarters]] | size = 1.3 million men | command_structure = [[File:SHAEF_Shoulder_Patch.svg|20px]] [[Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force|Allied Expeditionary Force]] | current_commander = | garrison = | ceremonial_chief = | colonel_of_the_regiment = | nickname = | patron = | motto = | colors = | march = | mascot = | battles = [[World War II]] | notable_commanders = [[Omar Bradley]] | anniversaries = }} The '''Twelfth United States [[Army group|Army Group]]''' was the largest and most powerful [[United States Army]] formation ever to take to the field, commanding four [[Field army|field armies]] at its peak in 1945: [[First United States Army]], [[United States Army Central|Third United States Army]], [[Ninth United States Army]], and [[Fifteenth United States Army]].{{cite book|isbn=978-0-671-41023-0|title=A General's Life|last=Bradley|first=Omar N.|authorlink=Omar Bradley|publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]]|year=1983|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/generalslifeaut00brad}} The [[order of battle]] across the four armies comprised 12 [[corps]], containing a total of 48 [[Division (military)|divisions]]. Formed eight days after the [[Normandy landings]], it initially controlled the First and the Third US Armies. Through various configurations in 1944 and 1945, the Twelfth US Army Group controlled the majority of American forces on the [[Western Front (World War II)|Western Front]]. It was commanded by General [[Omar Bradley]] with its headquarters established in London on 14 July 1944. During the first week of the Normandy landings and the [[Operation Overlord|Battle of Normandy]], Bradley's First US Army formed the right wing of the [[Allies of World War II|Allied]] lines. They were joined during July by the Third US Army, under the command of General [[George S. Patton]], to form the Twelfth Army Group. Twelfth Army Group became operational in France on 1 August 1944. With General Omar Bradley assuming command of the Twelfth Army Group, Lieutenant General [[Courtney Hodges]] assumed command of the First Army. In addition, the [[United States Army Air Forces|USAAF]]'s [[Ninth Air Force#Operations in Europe 1944–1945|Ninth Air Force]] (not included in the 1.3 million soldiers figure) was attached to support the field armies of the Twelfth Army Group. Until 1 September 1944, when [[Dwight D. Eisenhower|General Dwight D. Eisenhower]] assumed overall command of the Allied land forces in [[Western Front (World War II)|Northwest Europe]], the US forces in Normandy were included with the [[Second Army (United Kingdom)|British Second Army]] and the [[First Canadian Army]] in the British headquarters formation [[21st Army Group]], commanded by [[Bernard Montgomery|General Bernard Montgomery]]. After the breakout from the beach-head at Normandy, the Twelfth Army Group formed the center of the Allied forces on the Western Front. To the north was the British 21st Army Group (the First Canadian and British Second) and, to the south, advancing from their [[Operation Dragoon|landing]] on the Mediterranean coast, was the [[Sixth United States Army Group]] ([[United States Army Europe|Seventh United States Army]] and [[First Army (France)|French First Army]]). {{Military unit sidebar|title=U.S. Army Groups|previous=[[Sixth United States Army Group]]|next=[[15th Army Group]]}} As the Twelfth advanced through Germany in 1945, it grew to control four United States field armies: the [[First United States Army|First]], the [[United States Army Central|Third]], the [[Ninth United States Army|Ninth]] and the [[Fifteenth United States Army|Fifteenth]]. By [[Victory in Europe Day|V-E Day]], the Twelfth Army Group was a force that numbered over 1.3 million men.{{cite web |title=CSI Report No. 6, Larger units: Theater Army – Army Group – Field Army |date=January 1985 |website=Combat Studies Institute, U.S. Army Command and General Staff College, Fort Leavenworth, Kansas |url=https://permanent.fdlp.gov/websites/usacac.army.mil/Cac2/cgsc/carl/download/csipubs/csi6.pdf}} Twelfth Army Group was inactivated on 12 July 1945 upon Bradley's departure to become Director of the [[United States Department of Veterans Affairs|Veterans Administration]]. Its subordinate elements then became directly subordinate to [[United States Army Europe and Africa|United States Army Europe]]. ==Staff== [[File:Twelfth Army Group Staff.jpg|thumb|right|Omar Bradley and senior staff circa September 1944 - (L-to-R); Sibert, Kibler, Allen, Bradley, Moses, O'Hare]] {| class="wikitable" |+ Headquarters Twelfth United States Army Group
